candidate.tested_claim: Among the inspected Portalocker 3.x/4.0/4.1/4.2 sequence, 4.2.0 is the first release that combines the 4.0 raw-integer-descriptor byte-zero fix with the later low-level Windows fallback-LK and per-call-OVERLAPPED correctness fixes; therefore a policy that intends to exclude those known defects cannot set a floor below 4.2.0.

primary_source_checks.observed: Release notes explicitly say the Windows msvcrt locker previously locked from the current file position instead of byte 0 for raw file descriptors and that this could break mutual exclusion on files larger than 64KiB; v4.0.0 fixes it.
Release notes call 4.1.0 a documentation release and explicitly state that no runtime behaviour changed.

Official changelog records the 4.2 MsvcrtLocker fallback LK_* table correction; the prior shifted values could map LK_LOCK to LK_UNLCK. It also records that Win32Locker now creates a fresh OVERLAPPED for every LockFileEx/UnlockFileEx call instead of reusing one across calls and threads.
Current official source documents the corrected MsvcrtLocker fallback values and uses per-call Win32 OVERLAPPED objects, corroborating the changelog's low-level Windows-lock fixes.
